university: University of Colorado Denver/Anschutz Medical Campus

documents.unit: Student Conduct and Community Standards, CU Denver
documents.title: GenAI and Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule. It says authorization "is legitimate only if given by the faculty member", that students must "check with your faculty about AI use in their course", and that rules "may vary for each assignment"; it offers an AI Assessment Scale of four levels. A tiered, instructor-decided scheme makes the stance delegates, even though the fallback is "assume you DO NOT have permission".
documents.summary: CU Denver Student Conduct explains how the Academic Integrity Policy (7050) applies to generative AI: AI-completed work is likely cheating, uncredited AI work is plagiarism, and inaccurate or altered AI output can be fabrication or falsification. Faculty decide what is allowed, using a four-level AI Assessment Scale, and a student checklist covers ownership, verification, citation and ability to explain the work.

units.why: The page opens by binding every student to Campus Policy 7050: "All students are held to the University’s Academic Integrity Policy". The rule is compliance with an existing university policy (P77), not a framework with purpose and scope (P56).
units.resolution_why: A coded P77 (comply with existing university policy), B coded P56 (institution-wide framework, noting P77 as a second fit). The source sentence binds students to Policy 7050 and gives no principles, purpose or scope of its own, which is the P77 definition; P56 needs a stated framework. Final P77.
units.anchor: All students are held to the University’s Academic Integrity Policy
units.fit_note: Also frames this page as the practical application of the policy to GenAI (scope statement, P56).

units.why: "we expect ethical use of Generative AI" states a community expectation about AI in academic work. P95 (integrity culture of the community) fits better than P56 because it gives no purpose or scope, only an ethical expectation.
units.resolution_why: A coded P95/neutral, B coded P56/permit. The sentence only states a community expectation of ethical use; it gives no purpose, scope or principles (so not P56), and it says nothing that allows or bans particular uses, so unit_stance is neutral rather than permit. P95 (integrity culture of the community) is the nearest type. Final P95, neutral.
units.anchor: As a community we expect ethical use of Generative AI (GenAI) in your academic work
units.fit_note: Expectation of 'ethical use' implies AI use is possible, but no specific rule is stated.

units.why: The definition of cheating covers use of 'devices not authorized by the instructor'; it classifies unauthorized AI-type use as cheating, so P36.
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. The source defines cheating as use of materials or devices "not authorized by the instructor" on a page about GenAI, which classifies unauthorized use as cheating: a real policy statement. A did not code it. Kept as P36/informs; actor student because the page addresses students.
units.anchor: use of information, materials, notes, study aids, or other devices not authorized by the instructor
units.frag_start: involves the possession, communication, or use

units.why: The cheating definition says "Authorization is legitimate only if given by the faculty member", so the instructor alone decides what AI is authorized (P04). It is a decision-rights rule, not a tier list.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B student; both P04/informs/general. The sentence says authorization counts only when the responsible faculty member gives it, on a page addressed to students and binding what they can rely on, so actor is student. Final P04.
units.anchor: is legitimate only if given by the faculty member responsible for the evaluation

units.why: "Prompting Generative AI (GenAI) to complete a task, that has been assigned to you by a faculty member, is likely cheating" bars having AI do assigned work, which is P19 (do not have AI produce the work you submit). It also labels the act cheating (P36).
units.resolution_why: A coded P36 (cheating classification) with a fit note naming P19, B coded P19 with a note naming P36. The sentence names a specific act (prompting AI to complete an assigned task) and a consequence label. The act is what a reader looking for this rule would look up, and P19's definition states it directly, while P36 holds general classifications. Final P19; the cheating label is kept in fit_note.
units.anchor: that has been assigned to you by a faculty member, is likely cheating
units.fit_note: Also labels the act 'likely cheating' (misconduct classification, P36).

units.why: "By asking GenAI to do your work, your faculty member is unable to evaluate your learning" gives the reason for the ban as honest evaluation of learning. P95 (honest evaluation) rather than P41 (skill-building practice) because the stated harm is to evaluation.
units.anchor: your faculty member is unable to evaluate your learning
units.fit_note: Reason is that instructors cannot evaluate learning; touches on learning but is about evaluation.

units.why: "unless you have expressed permission from your faculty member, assume you DO NOT have permission to use GenAI" sets the default when no permission is given, so the fallback rule P06.
units.anchor: assume you DO NOT have permission to use GenAI

units.why: "Submitting work completed by GenAI without giving this source credit is plagiarism" makes failure to credit AI the violation. P28 (nondisclosure is the violation) fits because the trigger is missing credit; it is also a plagiarism classification (P36).
units.resolution_why: A coded P28, B coded P36 with a note that credit is implied (P24). The sentence's condition is 'without giving this source credit', so the violation is nondisclosure, which is P28's definition ('failure to disclose is itself the violation'). P36 would hold a plain misconduct label with no credit condition. Final P28; the plagiarism label is kept in fit_note.
units.anchor: Submitting work completed by GenAI without giving this source credit is plagiarism
units.fit_note: Also classifies the act as plagiarism (misconduct classification, P36).

units.why: "Making slights edits and changes to a GenAI output is considered mosaic plagiarism" classifies lightly edited AI output as misconduct, so P36.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase during-work and unit_stance prohibit, B coded when-misuse and restrict. The sentence names what counts as plagiarism, a misconduct definition like the neighbouring plagiarism sentence that both coders put in when-misuse. It does not ban AI use outright, since credited use is allowed elsewhere on the page, so restrict. Final when-misuse, restrict. Type P36 agreed.
units.anchor: Making slights edits and changes to a GenAI output is considered “mosaic plagiarism”

units.why: "You are responsible to find, ensure they are valid, and cite the original sources" tells students to verify and cite the original sources behind GenAI output. P31 (verify) is chosen because the main duty is validity; citing sources partly exceeds it.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B neutral; type P31, must, during-work agreed. The sentence puts a verify-and-cite duty on the student and does not itself allow or ban AI use, so neutral. The cite duty is kept in fit_note.
units.anchor: You are responsible to find, ensure they are valid, and cite the original sources
units.fit_note: Also requires citing the original sources behind AI output, not only verifying them. Adds a duty to cite the original sources beneath the AI output.

units.why: The MLA line gives the form of a ChatGPT citation: prompt text, version, OpenAI, date accessed, URL. That names tool, prompt and date, so P25.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality should with a policy that says students cite in MLA, B coded informs with no policy. The page only gives the format and does not say students must or should use MLA. Informs avoids strengthening the source; the anchor omits the word MLA, so a short policy names the format. Final informs with policy wording that stays within the source. Type P25 agreed.
units.anchor: “Your prompt text” prompt. ChatGPT, Version, OpenAI, Date accessed, URL.
units.policy: The MLA citation for ChatGPT is: “Your prompt text” prompt. ChatGPT, Version, OpenAI, Date accessed, URL.

units.why: The APA line gives the form of a ChatGPT citation with author, year, version and URL. It is a second citation format, so P25 again.
units.resolution_why: Same disagreement as the MLA line: A should with a policy saying students cite, B informs with no policy. The page only gives the APA format, so informs; a short policy names APA, which the anchor lacks. Type P25 agreed.
units.anchor: OpenAI. (2023) ChatGPT (May 3 version)[Large language model]. URL.
units.policy: The APA citation for ChatGPT is: OpenAI. (2023) ChatGPT (May 3 version)[Large language model]. URL.
units.fit_note: Gives the APA format (tool, version, year, URL) but not the prompt.

units.why: "Submitting work that is factually inaccurate from GenAI could be seen as a fabrication of information" classifies inaccurate AI output as a misconduct (fabrication), so P36.
units.anchor: factually inaccurate from GenAI could be seen as a fabrication of information
units.fit_note: Also says AI output may be inaccurate, so students must check it (P31).

units.why: "GenAI is known to produce hallucinated sources and results" is a fact that warns output is unreliable, so P31 with modality informs.
units.anchor: GenAI is known to produce "hallucinated" sources and results.

units.why: "Using GenAI to forge documents may also be a violation of the Student Code of Conduct" is a conduct rule against using AI to falsify records, so P74.
units.anchor: GenAI to forge documents may also be a violation of the Student Code of Conduct

units.why: "you are responsible to determine the validity of all sources that you use in academic tasks" puts verification on the student. P31 because it is a verify duty.
units.anchor: responsible to determine the validity of all sources that you use

units.why: "Instructing GenAI to alter, change, or skew results may be considered falsification" bans using AI to falsify data. P74 (falsify data) fits its definition; it is also misconduct (P36) but the act described is falsification.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase during-work, B general; type P74 and must-not agreed. The act (instructing AI to alter results) happens while doing work, like the earlier unit on prompting AI to complete a task, so during-work. Final during-work.
units.anchor: Instructing GenAI to alter, change, or skew results may be considered falsification

units.why: "You are responsible to uphold ethical standards while a student" is a general duty of ethical conduct. It fits P29 only partly because it is not about submitted work.
units.anchor: You are responsible to uphold ethical standards while a student
units.fit_note: General ethical-standards duty, not ownership of submitted work. Responsibility for ethical standards in general rather than for submitted work specifically.

units.why: "It is your responsibility to check with your faculty about AI use in their course" makes the student responsible for learning each course's AI rule, so P78 (not P10, which is about asking when unsure).
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to check with your faculty about AI use in their course

units.why: "Be aware this may vary for each assignment" says AI rules can differ by assignment, so the decision sits at the assignment level (P04).
units.resolution_why: A coded phase course-start, B general. The sentence "Be aware this may vary for each assignment" states a fact about where the AI rule is set, not an act of communicating expectations; the preceding sentence carries the course-start duty. Final general. Type P04 agreed.
units.anchor: Be aware this may vary for each assignment

units.why: The "AI Assessment Scale" table sets four named levels of AI use (No AI, Plan, Collaborate, Create), which is the definition of P05.
units.resolution_why: A coded the scale as its own P05 unit (general, actor all) and coded the No AI row separately; B coded one P05 unit anchored on the No AI row (during-work, student). The scale as a whole is a naming-of-tiers statement, not a task-time act, so it is anchored on its heading, phase general, actor all, and the No AI row is kept as its own unit (A only). The policy wording says 'the page’s' rather than 'the university’s' because the source is the Student Conduct office page.
units.anchor: AI Assessment Scale
units.policy: The page’s AI Assessment Scale names four types of GenAI use: No AI, Plan with AI, Collaborate with AI and Create with AI.

units.why: The "No AI" level says the task is done "independently without any GenAI assistance". It is the ban level of the scale; P01 is closest, but it applies per task, so a fit note.
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. The No AI row of the AI Assessment Scale is a real policy statement: "The task is completed independently without any GenAI assistance". B folded it into its scale unit. Kept as its own unit; P01 is the nearest type, with a fit note because the ban applies only to tasks at this level.
units.anchor: The task is completed independently without any GenAI assistance
units.fit_note: A ban that applies only to tasks the instructor places at the No AI level, not by default.

units.why: The "Plan with AI" level allows GenAI for "brainstorming, outlining, or initial research" before the task. Brainstorming is P15.
units.anchor: GenAI may be used for pre-task activities such as brainstorming, outlining, or initial research
units.fit_note: Also allows outlining and initial research. Also covers outlining and initial research as pre-task activities.

units.why: The "Collaborate with AI" level lets GenAI help complete the task by "creating a draft, providing feedback, and grammar edits". Writing support is P91; it also allows idea generation, so a fit note.
units.resolution_why: Same type, actor, phase and modality; A wrote a normalized policy, B left it null. A's anchor omitted 'idea generation'. Final uses B's fuller anchor with A's policy, which carries the tier name the anchor lacks.
units.anchor: like idea generation, creating a draft, providing feedback, and grammar edits.
units.policy: At the Collaborate with AI level, GenAI is used to help complete the task, like idea generation, creating a draft, providing feedback, and grammar edits.
units.fit_note: Also covers idea generation and helping complete the task, beyond editing. Level also includes idea generation and creating a draft, broader than editing support.

units.why: The "Create with AI" level says GenAI "is used to complete an elements of the task", allowing AI-generated content for parts of a task. P16 (AI output under stated conditions); the condition is the instructor placing the task at this level.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all codes. A policy line was added because the anchor alone does not name the tier it belongs to; the source's typo 'an elements' is kept.
units.anchor: GenAI is used to complete an elements of the task.
units.policy: At the Create with AI level, GenAI is used to complete an elements of the task.
units.fit_note: Does not state conditions such as caps or citation; the tier itself is the condition. Describes the level only; no conditions on size or citation, and not specific to code.

units.why: The checklist intro, "To better ensure your work is your own", says students should be able to answer yes to each statement; it ties the checklist to owning the work (P29).
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. The checklist intro says students should be able to answer yes to the statements 'to better ensure your work is your own', a real statement that frames the checklist as a duty to own the work. Kept as P29/should, during-work.
units.anchor: To better ensure your work is your own, you should be able to confidently answer

units.why: "I have been permitted, by my faculty member, to use GenAI on this assignment" makes instructor permission a precondition for use, so the instructor decides (P04).
units.resolution_why: A coded P04/restrict, B coded P78/neutral. The item requires actual permission from the faculty member, so the decision sits with the instructor (P04) and AI use is allowed only with it (restrict). P78 is about finding out and following the rules; that is the next checklist item. Final P04, restrict.
units.anchor: I have been permitted, by my faculty member, to use GenAI on this assignment
units.fit_note: Frames instructor permission as a precondition checked by the student before submission.

units.why: "I understand the way in which I am permitted to use GenAI on this assignment" requires the student to know the permitted use, so P78.
units.anchor: I understand the way in which I am permitted to use GenAI on this assignment

units.why: "I am using my own thoughts, words, and tone of voice" says the submitted work must be the student's own, so P29.
units.anchor: I am using my own thoughts, words, and tone of voice

units.why: "I have checked sources, and properly cited any facts, statistics, or quotes to the original author" asks students to check and cite the underlying sources. P31 (verify) is nearest; citing exceeds it.
units.anchor: properly cited any facts, statistics, or quotes to the original author
units.fit_note: Also requires citing facts, statistics and quotes to the original author. Combines checking sources with citing them to the original author.

units.why: "I have analyzed the GenAI output and identified false, biased, and inaccurate information" is a verify-and-critically-evaluate duty, so P31.
units.anchor: analyzed the GenAI output and identified false, biased, and inaccurate

units.why: "I have documented how I used GenAI and have cited it properly" asks the student to document and cite AI use. Citing is the explicit duty in the sentence, which is P24; keeping a record is P26 only if it were submitted, which is not said.
units.resolution_why: A coded P26 (keep and submit logs), B coded P24 (disclose or cite with submission). The sentence says 'documented how I used' and 'cited it properly'; nothing says logs or transcripts are kept or submitted, which P26 requires, while citing and acknowledging use matches P24. Final P24; the documentation duty is kept in fit_note.
units.anchor: I have documented how I used GenAI and have cited it properly
units.fit_note: Also asks for documentation of how AI was used (close to P26); does not say it is submitted.

units.why: "I have not used confidential, protected, or copyrighted information" bars putting confidential or protected data into AI. P50 (protect confidential data) fits; the copyright part is P52, so a fit note.
units.resolution_why: A coded P50 (protect confidential data), B coded P49 (do not upload course materials). The item bars 'confidential, protected, or copyrighted information' and never mentions uploading or course materials, so P49 does not fit; confidential data is P50's core. The copyright part is kept in fit_note. Final P50.
units.anchor: I have not used confidential, protected, or copyrighted information
units.fit_note: Also covers copyrighted information (P52); does not say 'enter into AI' explicitly. Also covers confidential data (P50) and copyright (P52); the checklist does not say 'upload'.

units.why: "I can explain all my findings and demonstrate full understanding of the assignment without the aid of GenAI" requires students to explain and defend their work, so P30.
units.anchor: I can explain all my findings and demonstrate full understanding

units.why: "I can prove what sources I used and how I verified the information" requires students to keep proof of sources and verification. P31 is nearest; proof of process is partly P26.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase during-work, B when-misuse; type P31 agreed. This is a checklist item students check as they complete work; nothing in it ties it to suspicion or sanction. Final during-work.
units.anchor: I can prove what sources I used and how I verified the information
units.fit_note: Requires being able to prove sources and verification steps, a documentation duty beyond verifying. Adds that students must be able to prove their sources and verification process.

units.why: "doing it yourself imperfectly is the truest testament of learning" gives the learning reason for limiting AI: doing the work yourself builds skill (P41).
units.anchor: doing it yourself imperfectly is the truest testament of learning
units.fit_note: Frames it as a value statement, not a direct limit on AI.

notes: Single included document (university layer); school and computing layers none-found; course deferred. Source text has typos ('slights edits', 'an elements') kept verbatim. Policy 7050 itself and the TIPS tool page were not coded. Reconciled from coder A (35 units) and coder B (34 units).
